essays.your-training-app-doesnt-know-your-race-: Your Training App Doesn't Know Your Race Exists

rules: Composition only: never trace a photo or draw the source character; GG plays every role.
Captions use only claims and numbers from the essays; no coach, company or product named in the image.

formats.name: Two Buttons
formats.structure: Top panel: a hand hovers over two labelled red buttons. Bottom panel: the same man sweating, wiping his brow.
formats.mechanic: A dilemma where the right answer is obvious to everyone except the person choosing.
formats.feasibility_note: One character plus a two-button console and sweat drops.

hooks.section: Sweet Spot is Really Threshold
hooks.caption: Buttons: "Re-test my FTP honestly" / "Keep my best test ever". Bottom: GG sweating, label "Me, before 3×20 at 235 W".

formats.general_hook: Race week: "Ride the course recon" / "Do one more hard workout".
formats.risk_note: Layout is a page of Jake Clark's "Daily Struggle" webcomic: an artist's own work. He has not objected that we know of, but the earlier plan skipped it for this reason. Redraw composition only.

formats.name: Distracted Boyfriend
formats.structure: A man turns to stare at a passer-by while his partner glares at him. Each figure carries a label.
formats.mechanic: Temptation versus commitment: the thing you should want is right beside you and you are looking at the shiny one.
formats.feasibility_note: Three figures. Could be GG plus two objects (a power number and a course profile) to avoid drawing people.

hooks.section: Fitness Has a Shape
hooks.caption: GG: "Me". Passer-by: "FTP up 31 watts". Partner: "The course profile".

formats.general_hook: Off-season: GG eyeing a shiny new bike while "base miles" glares.
formats.risk_note: Stock photo by Antonio Guillem, who has objected to sexist reuse. Three real models. Do not draw the people; recreate the glance-and-glare composition only.

formats.name: Left Exit 12 Off Ramp
formats.structure: A highway sign shows "straight" and "exit" options; a car labelled "me" swerves hard onto the exit.
formats.mechanic: Choosing the worse option at the last second, with full knowledge.
formats.feasibility_note: One character on a bike, a road sign, a fork in a gravel road. Cycling-native.

hooks.section: Polarized Training is Just Better
hooks.caption: Sign, straight: "75–90% below LT1, 15–20% above LT2". Sign, exit: "Another block of Sweet Spot". GG on a bike, skidding onto the exit.

formats.general_hook: Race day: straight "Eat on schedule", exit "Eat when hungry".
formats.risk_note: Generic stock road scene; no person or character to recreate.

formats.name: UNO Draw 25
formats.structure: Panel 1: a card reading "Do X or draw 25". Panel 2: the person holding a huge fan of cards.
formats.mechanic: Someone would take any penalty rather than do one simple, sensible thing.
formats.feasibility_note: One character holding a card and a huge fan of cards (or gels).

hooks.section: The Part Where I Tell You Not to Buy Anything
hooks.caption: Card: "Practice your race-day fueling on every long ride, or draw 24 gels". Panel 2: GG holding a fan of 24 gels.

formats.general_hook: Taper: "Do less this week, or draw 25 extra intervals".
formats.risk_note: UNO is a Mattel trademark: do not draw the UNO logo or card design. A plain card with our type is fine.

formats.name: Waiting Skeleton
formats.structure: A skeleton sits on a bench covered in cobwebs. Caption: "Me waiting for X".
formats.mechanic: Waiting forever for something that is never coming.
formats.feasibility_note: One character drawn as (or turning into) a skeleton, a bench, cobwebs. A bike leaning on the bench sells it.

formats.name: Expanding Brain
formats.structure: Four stacked panels; each idea gets dumber while the brain glows brighter.
formats.mechanic: Irony: the glow rises as the reasoning falls apart.
formats.feasibility_note: One character, four head shots with increasing glow. Legibility at 390 px is the risk.

hooks.section: It's Conceptually Broken
hooks.caption: 1 "Ride 3 hours" · 2 "Ride for TSS" · 3 "Ride all of it at Sweet Spot for max TSS" · 4 "TSS is the metric, not the goal" (the brightest brain makes the sane point, flipping the joke).

formats.name: Scooby-Doo Mask Reveal
formats.structure: Panel 1: a hero grabs the villain's mask ("Let's see who you really are"). Panel 2: the mask is off, showing the real identity.
formats.mechanic: The scary or impressive thing was the boring thing all along.
formats.feasibility_note: Two roles. GG unmasks another GG, so one rig still covers it.

hooks.section: The Real Issue: Sweet Spot is Predatory Marketing
hooks.caption: Mask: "Training hack". Unmasked: "Marketing hack". GG: "Let's see who you really are."

formats.general_hook: Mask: "Secret race-winning workout". Unmasked: "Consistency".
formats.risk_note: Scooby-Doo characters are Warner Bros. IP: no Fred, no van, no ascot. Composition only.

formats.name: Epic Handshake
formats.structure: Two muscular forearms clasp. Each arm is labelled with a group and the grip is labelled with what they share.
formats.mechanic: Two groups who usually disagree turn out to agree on one thing.
formats.feasibility_note: Arms only, no faces. Easiest single-character format on the list.

hooks.section: Polarized Training is Just Better
hooks.caption: Left arm: "Competitive athletes: polarized". Right arm: "Recreational athletes: pyramidal". Grip: "Not threshold-heavy" (the 2025 network meta-analysis, 13 studies, 348 athletes).

formats.general_hook: "Coaches" + "Physiologists", grip: "Eat more on long rides".
formats.risk_note: From the film Predator, but only the arms are used and redrawn. No likeness.

formats.name: They're the Same Picture
formats.structure: Someone holds up two sheets: "Corporate needs you to find the differences between this picture and this picture." Reply: "They're the same picture."
formats.mechanic: Two things presented as different are identical.
formats.feasibility_note: One character holding two sheets.

hooks.section: Your Nervous System Treats Sweet Spot Like Threshold
hooks.caption: Sheets: "~90% FTP" and "~105% FTP". GG as your nervous system: "They're the same picture." (Seiler 2007: recovery cost essentially identical above LT1.)

formats.general_hook: "Rest day" vs "easy spin with the fast group": they're the same picture? (inverted).
formats.risk_note: From The Office (NBC); the real actress is Jenna Fischer. Do not draw her or the office set. Spider-Man pointing already used a sweet-spot-equals-threshold joke, so keep this one on the nervous-system section.

formats.name: Buff Doge vs. Cheems
formats.structure: Left: a muscular dog labelled with the strong past or option. Right: a small, weak dog labelled with the feeble one.
formats.mechanic: Exaggerated before/after or then/now contrast in body types.
formats.feasibility_note: The character twice, in two builds (needs a buff and a deflated variant of the rig).
